northern.January: Indoors: Start seeds for cool-season vegetables like broccoli and cabbage. Outdoors: Plan your garden layout.
northern.February: Indoors: Sow seeds for tomatoes and peppers. Outdoors: Plant bare-root roses and fruit trees if the ground isn't frozen.
northern.March: Plant cool-season crops like peas, spinach, and radishes as soon as the soil can be worked. Plant pansies for early color.
northern.April: Plant potatoes, lettuce, and carrots. It's time to transplant broccoli and cabbage seedlings outside.
northern.May: After the last frost, plant warm-season vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, squash, and beans. Plant annual flowers like marigolds and zinnias.
northern.June: Plant corn, cucumbers, and melons. Sow another round of bush beans for a continuous harvest. Deadhead annuals to encourage more blooms.
northern.July: Plant fall crops like kale and collard greens. Keep your garden well-watered during the summer heat.
northern.August: Sow seeds for fall harvests of lettuce, spinach, and radishes. Plant chrysanthemums for autumn color.
northern.September: Plant garlic and shallots for next year's harvest. It's a great time to plant new trees and shrubs.
northern.October: Plant spring-blooming bulbs like tulips, daffodils, and crocuses before the ground freezes. Clean up the garden and add compost.
northern.November: Protect tender plants from the coming cold. If you live in a mild climate, you can still plant garlic.
northern.December: Plan your garden for next year. Browse seed catalogs and dream of spring!

southern.January: Plant heat-loving vegetables like sweet potatoes, corn, and okra. Keep everything well-watered. Plant zinnias and celosia for vibrant summer color.
southern.February: Sow seeds for autumn vegetables like broccoli, cabbage, and cauliflower. Plant another round of beans and carrots.
southern.March: Plant leafy greens like spinach and lettuce. It's a great time to plant autumn-blooming flowers like asters and salvias.
southern.April: Plant garlic and onions for a winter harvest. Sow seeds for sweet peas to get fragrant spring flowers.
southern.May: Plant broad beans and peas. It's the perfect time to plant spring-blooming bulbs such as daffodils, tulips, and hyacinths.
southern.June: In frost-free areas, plant potatoes and onions. Plan your spring garden layout and order seeds.
southern.July: Indoors: Start seeds for tomatoes, peppers, and eggplants to get a head start on spring planting.
southern.August: Plant early spring vegetables like peas and spinach. Plant bare-root roses and deciduous trees.
southern.September: Plant potatoes, lettuce, and beetroot. As the soil warms up, it's time to plant summer-flowering bulbs like dahlias.
southern.October: It's prime time for planting summer vegetables like tomatoes, cucumbers, and zucchini. Plant petunias and marigolds for instant color.
southern.November: Plant corn, pumpkins, and melons. Keep an eye on watering as the weather gets warmer.
southern.December: Sow fast-growing crops like radishes and lettuce for a quick harvest. Keep your garden mulched to retain moisture.
